# Step 5 — verified model options and spending controls

Access date for all sources below: **2026-11-19**. Prices are USD, standard API rates unless stated otherwise. Public documentation was fetched; **no paid model, voice, telephony, or account-balance request was made**. These checks establish documented options, not access on this account or model quality.

## Existing client and compatibility

`src/voice_agent/models/llm.py` uses standard-library HTTP, not a provider SDK:

| Adapter / configured provider | Wire format | Tool calls and results |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI-compatible: `openai`, `groq`, `ollama` | `POST /chat/completions` below the configured base URL | Request `tools[].type=function`, JSON Schema parameters; assistant `tool_calls[].function.{name,arguments}` with JSON-string arguments; replies use `role=tool` and `tool_call_id`. |
| `anthropic` | `POST /v1/messages` | `tools[].input_schema`; assistant `tool_use` blocks with object `input`; user `tool_result` blocks with `tool_use_id`. Parallel results share one user turn. |

The internal message format normalizes tools to `{id,name,arguments}`. Malformed function-argument JSON becomes `_unparsed` for sandbox validation. Chat Completions JSON mode is supported; it is not a substitute for Step 4 verdict validation. Anthropic's `json_mode` argument has no implementation. There is no Responses, streaming, Realtime/WebRTC/WebSocket, STT, TTS, LiveKit or telephony implementation.

**Wire compatibility does not authorize spending.** Paid execution is now restricted to the exact direct OpenAI Chat Completions endpoint and an explicitly approved, priced text batch. Groq, Anthropic, custom remote endpoints, hosted tools, images and audio are blocked. Their adapters remain available for offline wire-format tests. Local Ollama remains available at loopback port 11434, with zero automatic retries. HTTP redirects are disabled.

## Verified models and prices

### Affordable text candidate for the first diagnostic

Source: [GPT-4o mini](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-4o-mini), cross-checked against [official API pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing).

- Pin **`gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18`**, not the moving alias `gpt-4o-mini`.
- Input **$0.15 / 1 million text tokens**; output **$0.60 / 1 million text tokens**. Cached input is $0.075 / million; the ledger deliberately assumes **no cache discount**.
- Documented context window: **128,000 tokens**. Documented model output maximum: **16,384 tokens**. Application output maximum: **1,200 tokens**, including tool-call arguments.
- Chat Completions, function calling and structured outputs are documented. The client now sends `max_completion_tokens`, `n=1`, and `service_tier="default"` to direct OpenAI.
- [Chat Completions reference](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat/subresources/completions/methods/create): `max_completion_tokens` bounds generated tokens; `max_tokens` is deprecated. Exact live parameter acceptance and account access remain untested.
- **The official page marks this snapshot deprecated.** This is a low-cost compatibility/calibration candidate, not a long-term model commitment. If unavailable, stop; do not silently substitute a model, endpoint or price. No nondeprecated text replacement was selected or certified in this step.

For comparison, [GPT-4.1 mini](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-4.1-mini), snapshot `gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14`, is documented at $0.40 input / $1.60 output per million text tokens, 1,047,576 context, and is also marked deprecated. It is **not enabled** in the cost ledger. Model choice and judge accuracy still need calibration, not inference from price or schema validity.

### Feasible speech options by documentation — execution remains blocked

All token prices in this table are **per 1 million tokens**, not per minute. No audio model is enabled in the ledger.

| Purpose and exact ID | Documented price | Status / qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Direct speech-to-speech candidate: [`gpt-realtime-2.1-mini`](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-realtime-2.1-mini) | Text input/output **$0.60 / $2.40**; audio input/output **$10 / $20**. Cached input: text $0.06, audio $0.30. | Official default snapshot has the same ID; no separate dated snapshot listed. Audio/text input and output, function calling, 128,000 context and 32,000 max output tokens documented. This stays within the approved direct OpenAI Realtime family; it is a candidate, not a new deployment. |
| Original Realtime reference: [`gpt-realtime-2025-08-28`](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-realtime), alias `gpt-realtime` | Text input/output **$4 / $16**; audio input/output **$32 / $64**; cached input $0.40 for both. | Deprecated. LiveKit plugin's documented default is still `gpt-realtime`; future setup must select a reviewed model explicitly, not inherit that default. |
| Separate STT: [`gpt-transcribe`](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-transcribe) | **$0.0045 / audio minute**, model page's audio-duration pricing unit. | File and Realtime input transcription documented. Default snapshot has the same ID. Not integrated or enabled. |
| Separate STT comparison: [`gpt-4o-mini-transcribe-2025-12-15`](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-4o-mini-transcribe) | Model/pricing tables list **$1.25 input / $5 output per million tokens**; pricing page estimates **$0.003 / minute**. | Deprecated; transcription guide gives shutdown **2027-02-26**. Do not turn the estimated minute rate into a hard token-cost bound. |
| Separate STT fallback: [`whisper-1`](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/whisper-1) | **$0.006 / minute** | Deprecated; documented shutdown **2027-02-26**. |
| Separate TTS: [`gpt-4o-mini-tts-2025-12-15`](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-4o-mini-tts) | **$0.60 / million text input tokens**, **$12 / million audio output tokens** | Deprecated; TTS guide gives shutdown **2027-01-06**. Not a long-term recommendation. |
| Separate TTS fallback: [`tts-1`](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/tts-1) | **$15 / 1 million input characters** | Character pricing is not token pricing. Deprecated; documented shutdown **2027-01-06**. |

Additional official sources: [STT guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/speech-to-text), [TTS guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/text-to-speech), [Realtime cost guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/realtime-costs), [API pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing).

Separate STT → text agent → TTS is an alternative architecture, not an automatic extra charge in a direct speech-to-speech session. Optional Realtime input transcription can add charges. The Realtime cost guide describes approximate audio-token rates and repeated history per response; **input duration alone does not bound output, repeated context, response count, retries or optional transcription**. Newer reasoning-capable Realtime models need model-specific accounting as well. Therefore the present hard audio limit is **0 seconds / 0 audio requests**. The $4 allocation is not permission to run an unbounded session.

## Local development and LiveKit readiness

Actual checks are in `evidence/step5/environment.json` and `environment-followup.json`:

- Python 3.15.2 is available. No Ollama executable or responding `/api/tags` at `127.0.0.1:11434`; no Ollama or LM Studio app found in `/Applications`.
- No `livekit-server` or `lk` executable; `127.0.0.1:7880` refused connection. Python distributions `livekit`, `livekit-agents`, `livekit-plugins-openai`, `openai` and `tiktoken` are absent in this interpreter.
- Docker is available/running, but no matching local-model/LiveKit container was found. Other running services were left untouched.
- OpenAI key presence was checked without displaying its value. LiveKit/Deepgram/Cartesia configuration was absent in the checked environment. Presence is not authentication or a credit-balance check.
- No runtime, SDK or model weights were installed or downloaded. Use deterministic oracle/sandbox checks and mocked completions now. Do not call a remote API and label it a local test. After a truly local Ollama model is installed, a local caller or judge can share a run with paid roles; only paid attempts enter the currency ledger. Do not route “local” endpoints to paid cloud models.

[LiveKit local setup](https://docs.livekit.io/transport/self-hosting/local/) documents `brew install livekit`, then `livekit-server --dev`, bound to `127.0.0.1:7880` by default. These commands were **not** run. Development credentials in that page are public examples, not production credentials.

[LiveKit OpenAI Realtime plugin](https://docs.livekit.io/agents/models/realtime/plugins/openai/) documents the direct plugin with `OPENAI_API_KEY`, Python installation `livekit-agents[openai]~=1.8`, and distinguishes it from **LiveKit Inference**, which uses LiveKit credentials and is billed by LiveKit Cloud. The current Python 3.15 environment's package compatibility is not verified; do not install dependencies blindly.

**Cost ownership:** local self-hosting does not use LiveKit Cloud session allowances, but still uses local compute/network resources. Hosted servers, LiveKit Cloud transport/agent hosting/Inference, Deepgram, Cartesia, SIP carriers, phone numbers and telephony minutes have separate billing. **The $20 OpenAI credit does not pay those bills.** [LiveKit pricing](https://livekit.io/pricing) advertises 1,000 free agent-session minutes monthly, but this does not mean unlimited free transport, inference or telephony; plan eligibility, quotas and overages were not activated or verified. No Cloud plan or non-OpenAI service is approved. Deepgram/Cartesia and all real outbound calls remain deferred.

## Ledger and enforcement

Canonical file: **`experiments/cost_ledger.json`**. Starting credit is the user's reported $20, not an authenticated balance or verified expiry. These are planning ceilings, not per-batch authorization:

| Allocation | Ceiling | Approved paid batches | Recorded usage / unresolved reservations |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Smoke tests/calibration | $1 | 0 | $0 / $0 |
| Text development, including caller and judge | $9 | 0 | $0 / $0 |
| Audio experiments | $4 | 0 | $0 / $0 |
| Held-out evaluation | $4 | 0 | $0 / $0 |
| Reserve — explicit approval only | $2 | 0 | $0 / $0 |
| **Total** | **$20** | **0** | **$0 / $0; $20 estimated remaining** |

`CostLedger` uses Decimal arithmetic, a cross-process lock and atomic replacement. Each save syncs the ledger file and directory. A reservation is persisted **before each actual HTTP attempt**. No SDK retry or redirect can send an uncounted request. Lock/sync/write errors fail closed. There is only **one in-flight paid request across the ledger**; unresolved pending requests block later sends, including after a crash or failed halt update. Recovery needs reconciliation, not deletion/reset of the ledger. A new run ID does not reset budget or request counts.

Requirements for a paid request:

1. Batch exists, is explicitly approved, and has a nonempty approval reference to the user's authorization. The current proposed batch has `approved=false`; all paid calls are blocked.
2. Exact model matches its catalog entry; endpoint is direct OpenAI Chat Completions; text-only, one completion, standard/default tier, local function tools only. Returned model and tier must match before usage reconciliation.
3. Reserve **full documented input context × uncached input rate + capped output × output rate**. This is intentionally larger than an expected bill and needs no tokenizer guess. The request-byte limit is a separate payload-size cap, **not** a claimed token-count estimator.
4. Check global credit, allocation, batch dollar cap, request count and retry count under the same lock. Each HTTP retry consumes another request and reservation, even if no response arrives.
5. Reconcile only real nonnegative integer `prompt_tokens` and `completion_tokens` within reserved bounds. Cached discounts are ignored. Failed/lost requests keep the full reservation; missing/invalid usage or unexpected model/tier halts the batch. Nonretryable/malformed successful responses halt too. Errors remain infrastructure/evaluation issues, not ordinary zero-reward model failures.

| Limit | Hard application maximum | Proposed first smoke |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Paid HTTP attempts across agent/caller/judge/retries | 100 per batch, plus dollar ceilings | **4 total** |
| Output tokens, including tool arguments | 1,200/request | Caller 200, agent ≤800 each, judge ≤1,200; hard global cap 1,200 |
| Input | Model's documented 128,000-token context upper bound used for reservation; serialized request ≤256,000 bytes | ≤64,000 serialized bytes; reserve all 128,000 input tokens regardless |
| Caller generations | ≤12/episode; paid batch can lower it | Diagnostic has one caller generation; outer pipeline cap remains 12 |
| Agent tool rounds | 8/caller turn | Diagnostic has one read-only tool result |
| Actual executed tool calls, including parallel calls | ≤8/caller turn; paid batch can lower it | Runtime hard cap 8; diagnostic exposes one read-only tool |
| HTTP retries | ≤1, each separately reserved; default 0 | **0** |
| Audio | **0 seconds / 0 requests** | **0** |

The generic M3 pipeline accepts `--budget-batch APPROVED_BATCH_ID` and passes the same ledger to all roles. It records batch IDs in new run manifests. Do **not** use a full ten-task pipeline as the proposed four-request diagnostic. Historic `tokens_*_agent_plus_simulator` summary fields still exclude the judge by design; the **cost ledger**, not those fields, is the accounting source for all paid roles and retries. Local-model usage is separate, zero-provider-cost development usage, with existing finite episode/turn/tool loops.

Limits are application-side bounds for this project's one canonical ledger. They do not cover API-key use outside this client, another checkout/ledger, external account spending, taxes, price changes or a provider violating requested model/tier/token limits. Unexpected model/tier usage could already have been billed before the response is checked. Verify prices again before approving later batches, and check the provider balance/expiry separately. No provider-console hard cap was configured or claimed. Filesystem durability depends on the OS/device honoring sync operations; this is not a multi-file transaction or a hardware power-loss test. Approval references are audit records, not cryptographic proof of human authorization; automation must never self-approve or edit ceilings to bypass a refusal.

## Proposed next paid action — approval required

**Batch `step5_smoke_001`: synthetic four-request text diagnostic, maximum authorization $0.10 from the $1 smoke allocation.**

1. One caller request: generate a single synthetic Solar question (≤200 output tokens).
2. One agent request: request a read-only `search_docs`-style local function (≤800 output tokens). Expose no CRM write/export tool.
3. Execute at most that one local read-only function, then one agent follow-up request using its result (≤800 output tokens). Stop early on malformed/missing tool calls; do not generate extra requests to “fix” them.
4. One judge request: return the complete structured verdict for the diagnostic's explicit rubric (≤1,200 output tokens). Validate it with Step 4 validation. This is a compatibility/calibration check, **not a regrade or held-out score**.

Purpose: confirm snapshot access, bounded Chat Completions parameters, function-call round trip, caller behavior, structured-judge parsing and usage accounting. Retain actual prompts/messages, raw responses, verdict attempts, command/log/exit status and ledger entries in a **new** run directory. No original scenario labels or human adjudications change. There will be no retry, audio or telephone call.

Conservative uniform bound (even though not every request uses 1,200 output tokens):

```text
per attempt = (128,000 × $0.15 + 1,200 × $0.60) / 1,000,000
            = $0.019920
four attempts = $0.079680 < $0.100000 authorization ceiling
```

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from contextlib import contextmanager
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation, localcontext
from pathlib import Path

try:
    import fcntl
except ImportError:  # No safe cross-process locking on this platform.
    fcntl = None

from voice_agent.utils.common import write_json


class BudgetError(RuntimeError):
    """The ledger is invalid, unavailable, or cannot authorize a request."""


def _money(value):
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise BudgetError("Money must be a decimal string")
    try:
        amount = Decimal(value)
    except InvalidOperation as exc:
        raise BudgetError("Invalid money") from exc
    if not amount.is_finite() or amount < 0:
        raise BudgetError("Money must be finite and nonnegative")
    return amount


def _int(value, minimum, maximum=None):
    if type(value) is not int or value < minimum or (maximum is not None and value > maximum):
        raise BudgetError("Invalid integer limit or token count")
    return value


def _price(model):
    if not isinstance(model, dict):
        raise BudgetError("Invalid model catalog entry")
    try:
        return (_money(model["input_usd_per_million"]),
                _money(model["output_usd_per_million"]),
                _int(model["max_input_tokens"], 1))
    except KeyError as exc:
        raise BudgetError("Incomplete model catalog entry") from exc


def max_cost_usd(model: str, max_output_tokens: int, catalog: dict) -> Decimal:
    """Price the entire input context and requested output at uncached rates."""
    try:
        input_price, output_price, max_input = _price(catalog[model])
        _int(max_output_tokens, 1, 1200)
        return (input_price * max_input + output_price * max_output_tokens) / Decimal(1_000_000)
    except (KeyError, TypeError) as exc:
        raise BudgetError("Unknown model") from exc


def _usage_cost(usage, model, max_output):
    if not isinstance(usage, dict):
        raise BudgetError("Missing usage")
    input_price, output_price, max_input = _price(model)
    try:
        prompt = _int(usage["prompt_tokens"], 0, max_input)
        completion = _int(usage["completion_tokens"], 0, max_output)
    except KeyError as exc:
        raise BudgetError("Missing usage tokens") from exc
    return (input_price * prompt + output_price * completion) / Decimal(1_000_000)


def _limits(batch):
    limits = batch.get("limits")
    if not isinstance(limits, dict):
        raise BudgetError("Missing limits")
    for name, low, high in (("max_requests", 1, 100), ("max_output_tokens", 1, 1200),
                            ("max_request_bytes", 1, 256000), ("max_retries", 0, 1),
                            ("max_caller_turns", 1, 12), ("max_tool_steps", 1, 8),
                            ("max_audio_seconds", 0, 0)):
        if name not in limits:
            raise BudgetError("Missing limit: " + name)
        _int(limits[name], low, high)
    return limits

    def __init__(self, path: Path, batch_id: str):
        self.path = Path(path)

    def _locked(self):
        if fcntl is None:
            raise BudgetError("Cross-process locking unavailable")
        try:
            with self.path.with_name(self.path.name + ".lock").open("a") as lock:
                fcntl.flock(lock.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
                try:
                    with localcontext() as ctx:
                        ctx.prec = 256
                        yield
                finally:
                    fcntl.flock(lock.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)

            with self.path.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:

            credit = _money(data["starting_credit_usd"])
            allocations = {name: _money(value) for name, value in data["allocations"].items()}
            batches = data["batches"]
            if any(not isinstance(batch, dict) for batch in batches):

                if batch.get("allocation") not in allocations:

                    raise BudgetError("Batch ceiling exceeds allocation or credit")

                    raise BudgetError("Unknown model")

        except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as exc:

    def _totals(self, data, credit):

        allocation_costs = {name: Decimal(0) for name in data["allocations"]}

            subtotal = Decimal(0)

            for request in batch["requests"]:

                    except BudgetError:

            allocation_costs[batch["allocation"]] += subtotal
        data["totals"] = {"recorded_usage_usd": str(recorded), "unreconciled_max_usd": str(held),

                    or total + cost > credit):

            if any(r["id"] == request_id for r in batch["requests"]):
                raise BudgetError("Duplicate request ID")
            batch["requests"].append({"id": request_id, "model": model, "role": role,
                                      "attempt": attempt, "timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),

    def _finish(self, request_id, usage=None, error_type=None):
        with self._locked():

    if type(value) is not int or value < minimum or (maximum is not None and value > maximum):
        raise BudgetError("Invalid integer limit or token count")
    return value


def _price(model):
    if not isinstance(model, dict):
        raise BudgetError("Invalid model catalog entry")
    try:
        return (_money(model["input_usd_per_million"]),
                _money(model["output_usd_per_million"]),
                _int(model["max_input_tokens"], 1))
    except KeyError as exc:
        raise BudgetError("Incomplete model catalog entry") from exc


def max_cost_usd(model: str, max_output_tokens: int, catalog: dict) -> Decimal:
    """Price the entire input context and requested output at uncached rates."""
    try:
        input_price, output_price, max_input = _price(catalog[model])
        _int(max_output_tokens, 1, 1200)
        return (input_price * max_input + output_price * max_output_tokens) / Decimal(1_000_000)
    except (KeyError, TypeError) as exc:
        raise BudgetError("Unknown model") from exc


def _usage_cost(usage, model, max_output):
    if not isinstance(usage, dict):
        raise BudgetError("Missing usage")
    input_price, output_price, max_input = _price(model)
    try:
        prompt = _int(usage["prompt_tokens"], 0, max_input)
        completion = _int(usage["completion_tokens"], 0, max_output)
    except KeyError as exc:
        raise BudgetError("Missing usage tokens") from exc
    return (input_price * prompt + output_price * completion) / Decimal(1_000_000)


def _limits(batch):
    limits = batch.get("limits")
    if not isinstance(limits, dict):
        raise BudgetError("Missing limits")
    for name, low, high in (("max_requests", 1, 100), ("max_output_tokens", 1, 1200),
                            ("max_request_bytes", 1, 256000), ("max_retries", 0, 1),
                            ("max_caller_turns", 1, 12), ("max_tool_steps", 1, 8),
                            ("max_audio_seconds", 0, 0)):
        if name not in limits:
            raise BudgetError("Missing limit: " + name)
        _int(limits[name], low, high)
    return limits

    def __init__(self, path: Path, batch_id: str):
        self.path = Path(path)
        self.batch_id = batch_id

    @contextmanager
    def _locked(self):
        if fcntl is None:
            raise BudgetError("Cross-process locking unavailable")
        try:
            with self.path.with_name(self.path.name + ".lock").open("a") as lock:
                fcntl.flock(lock.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
                try:
                    with localcontext() as ctx:
                        ctx.prec = 256
                        yield
                finally:
                    fcntl.flock(lock.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)
        except (OSError, InvalidOperation, OverflowError) as exc:
            raise BudgetError("Ledger lock or I/O failed") from exc

    def _load(self):
        try:
            with self.path.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                data = json.load(handle)
            if not isinstance(data, dict) or not isinstance(data["models"], dict) or not isinstance(data["allocations"], dict) or not isinstance(data["batches"], list):
                raise BudgetError("Invalid ledger")
            credit = _money(data["starting_credit_usd"])
            allocations = {name: _money(value) for name, value in data["allocations"].items()}
            batches = data["batches"]
            if any(not isinstance(batch, dict) for batch in batches):
                raise BudgetError("Invalid batch")
            ids = [batch.get("id") for batch in batches]
            if any(not isinstance(item, str) or not item for item in ids) or len(set(ids)) != len(ids):
                raise BudgetError("Invalid batch IDs")
            matches = [batch for batch in batches if batch["id"] == self.batch_id]
            if len(matches) != 1:
                raise BudgetError("Batch not found")
            target = matches[0]
            if target.get("approved") is not True or not isinstance(target.get("approval_reference"), str) or not target["approval_reference"].strip():
                raise BudgetError("Batch is not approved")
            for batch in batches:
                if batch.get("allocation") not in allocations:
                    raise BudgetError("Unknown allocation")
                ceiling = _money(batch["max_cost_usd"])
                if ceiling > allocations[batch["allocation"]] or ceiling > credit:
                    raise BudgetError("Batch ceiling exceeds allocation or credit")
                if batch.get("model") not in data["models"]:
                    raise BudgetError("Unknown model")
                _price(data["models"][batch["model"]])
                _limits(batch)
                if not isinstance(batch.get("requests"), list):
                    raise BudgetError("Invalid requests")
            return data, target, credit, allocations
        except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as exc:
            raise BudgetError("Cannot read valid ledger") from exc

    def _totals(self, data, credit):
        recorded = Decimal(0)
        held = Decimal(0)
        batch_costs = {}
        allocation_costs = {name: Decimal(0) for name in data["allocations"]}
        for batch in data["batches"]:
            subtotal = Decimal(0)
            seen = set()
            for request in batch["requests"]:
                if not isinstance(request, dict) or not isinstance(request.get("id"), str) or request["id"] in seen:
                    raise BudgetError("Invalid request entry")
                seen.add(request["id"])
                reservation = _money(request.get("reserve_max_cost_usd"))
                # Never trust a stored reservation smaller than the full-context price.
                maximum = _int(request.get("max_output_tokens"), 1, batch["limits"]["max_output_tokens"])
                required = max_cost_usd(batch["model"], maximum, data["models"])
                if reservation < required:
                    raise BudgetError("Reservation below full-context cost")
                cost = reservation
                if request.get("status") == "reconciled":
                    try:
                        cost = _usage_cost(request.get("usage"), data["models"][batch["model"]], maximum)
                    except BudgetError:
                        held += reservation
                    else:
                        recorded += cost
                else:
                    held += reservation
                subtotal += cost
            batch_costs[batch["id"]] = subtotal
            allocation_costs[batch["allocation"]] += subtotal
        data["totals"] = {"recorded_usage_usd": str(recorded), "unreconciled_max_usd": str(held),
                          "remaining_credit_estimate_usd": str(credit - recorded - held)}
        return batch_costs, allocation_costs, recorded + held

    @property
    def limits(self):
        with self._locked():
            _, batch, _, _ = self._load()
            return dict(_limits(batch))

    def reserve(self, model: str, max_output_tokens: int, request_bytes: int, role: str, attempt: int) -> str:
        with self._locked():

                raise BudgetError("Model or role not permitted")

            _int(request_bytes, 0, limits["max_request_bytes"])

                raise BudgetError("Request count exceeded")

            cost = max_cost_usd(model, max_output_tokens, data["models"])
            if (batch_costs[batch["id"]] + cost > _money(batch["max_cost_usd"])
                    or allocation_costs[batch["allocation"]] + cost > allocations[batch["allocation"]]
                    or total + cost > credit):

            request_id = f"{self.batch_id}-{len(batch['requests']) + 1}"
            if any(r["id"] == request_id for r in batch["requests"]):
                raise BudgetError("Duplicate request ID")
            batch["requests"].append({"id": request_id, "model": model, "role": role,
                                      "attempt": attempt, "timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
                                      "max_output_tokens": max_output_tokens, "request_bytes": request_bytes,
                                      "reserve_max_cost_usd": str(cost), "status": "pending"})

            write_json(self.path, data)

    def _finish(self, request_id, usage=None, error_type=None):
        with self._locked():
            data, batch, credit, _ = self._load()
            self._totals(data, credit)
            matches = [request for request in batch["requests"] if request["id"] == request_id]
            if len(matches) != 1 or matches[0].get("status") != "pending":
                raise BudgetError("Request not pending")
            request = matches[0]
            error = None
            if error_type is not None:
                request.update(status="failed", error_type=error_type)
            else:
                try:
                    _usage_cost(usage, data["models"][batch["model"]], request["max_output_tokens"])
                except BudgetError as exc:
                    request.update(status="failed", error_type="invalid_usage")
                    error = exc
                else:
                    request.update(status="reconciled", usage={"prompt_tokens": usage["prompt_tokens"],
                                                               "completion_tokens": usage["completion_tokens"]})
            self._totals(data, credit)
            write_json(self.path, data)
            if error:
                raise error

    def reconcile(self, request_id: str, usage: dict) -> None:
        self._finish(request_id, usage=usage)

    def fail(self, request_id: str, error_type: str) -> None:
        if not isinstance(error_type, str) or not error_type or len(error_type) > 100 or not all(c.isalnum() or c in "_-" for c in error_type):
            raise BudgetError("Invalid error type")
        self._finish(request_id, error_type=error_type)

Chat Completions parameter reference: https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat/subresources/completions/methods/create

Research verified `max_completion_tokens` as an output upper bound, `max_tokens` deprecated, and standard/default tier selection. Parameter acceptance and actual billing were not exercised.

## Current Realtime candidate

> Output modalities: text, audio

> Reasoning token support

Text-token table per 1M tokens: input $0.6; cached input $0.06; output $2.4.
Audio-token table per 1M tokens: input $10; cached input $0.3; output $20.
Realtime endpoint supported; Chat Completions and separate speech-generation/transcription endpoints not supported for this model. No separate dated snapshot is listed. Image rates are not used because image requests are blocked.

## Current separate STT option

URL: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-transcribe

> Model ID: `gpt-transcribe`
> Default snapshot: `gpt-transcribe`

Transcription audio-duration table: $0.0045 / minute. File transcription and Realtime transcription endpoints supported. This is a documented option, not an integration or approved audio batch.

## Separate STT/TTS comparisons

Pricing URL: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing

- `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`: input $1.25, output $5.00, estimated $0.003 / minute. Do not convert an estimate into a hard cap.
- `gpt-4o-mini-tts`: audio output $12.00 / 1M tokens; text input $0.60 / 1M tokens.
- `tts-1`: $15.00 / 1M input characters.
- Whisper: $0.006 / minute.

Model snapshots/status and announced shutdown dates were checked by the research agent against the model pages and these guides:
https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/speech-to-text
https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/text-to-speech

Retain the deprecation warnings in `model_and_spending_plan.md`; none of these comparisons enables a paid model. Realtime cost-guide URL: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/realtime-costs . Audio-token approximations and history replay do not yield a hard total-spend bound from input duration alone.

## LiveKit billing boundary

URL: https://docs.livekit.io/agents/models/realtime/plugins/openai/

> With LiveKit Inference, you use your LiveKit Cloud credentials instead of a separate OpenAI API key, and LiveKit Cloud bills you for usage. Use the plugin instead if you want to manage your own billing.

> Use the OpenAI plugin to connect directly to the OpenAI Realtime API with your own API key.

Python install shown: `uv add "livekit-agents[openai]~=1.8"`. This was not run. The plugin model default is documented as `gpt-realtime`; do not confuse that legacy default with the newer candidate above. The current Inference table includes `openai/gpt-realtime-2.1-mini`, but Inference would bill LiveKit, not the user's OpenAI credit.

URL: https://docs.livekit.io/transport/self-hosting/local/

macOS install example: `brew update && brew install livekit`; development server: `livekit-server --dev`. Default bind: `127.0.0.1:7880`. No install/server startup was performed.

URL: https://livekit.io/pricing

> No credit card required • 1,000 free agent session minutes monthly

This advertisement is not proof of plan activation, unlimited transport/inference or telephony coverage. No LiveKit Cloud, Deepgram, Cartesia or carrier allocation was approved. OpenAI credit is separate.

No paid batch, provider authentication, live model/voice run, human adjudication or real outbound call was performed. **Project provider spend: $0.** Semantic judge quality, real-provider behavior and low-level HTTP retry accounting remain unverified; the $20 budget and approval before each paid batch still apply.

## Step 5 — Model verification and spending controls

**Status: official model/pricing checks complete; cost controls tested offline. Stopped pending approval for the first paid text diagnostic.** Full model IDs, URLs, access dates, units, compatibility and limitations: [`model_and_spending_plan.md`](model_and_spending_plan.md).

### Choices and environment

- Access date **2026-11-19**. Affordable text diagnostic candidate: **`gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18`**, $0.15 input / $0.60 output per million text tokens, 128,000 context. It is **deprecated**; live access and exact parameter acceptance are not assumed. No silent fallback model is allowed.
- Verified direct Realtime candidate **`gpt-realtime-2.1-mini`**: text $0.60/$2.40 and audio $10/$20 input/output per million tokens. Separate STT **`gpt-transcribe`**: $0.0045/audio minute. Legacy mini-transcribe, mini-TTS, Whisper and tts-1 IDs/prices and deprecation/shutdown warnings are recorded separately. These are documented options, not live voice tests or enabled models.
- Existing clients cover OpenAI-compatible function-tool messages for OpenAI/Groq/Ollama and Anthropic tool-use/result blocks. Responses, Realtime, STT/TTS and LiveKit are not implemented. Remote execution is now gated to priced, approved direct OpenAI text requests; other paid providers, hosted tools, images and audio are blocked.
- No available Ollama endpoint/executable/cache, local model app, LiveKit server/CLI or corresponding Python packages in the checked environment. Docker is running without matching model/LiveKit containers. Nothing was installed, downloaded or started. Development used deterministic fixtures/oracle and mocked model completions.
- Official LiveKit docs distinguish local self-hosting + direct OpenAI plugin from LiveKit Cloud Inference billing. OpenAI credit does **not** cover LiveKit, Deepgram, Cartesia or telephony. No separate service or real outbound call is approved.

### Budget contract

- Canonical ledger: **`experiments/cost_ledger.json`**. Planning ceilings: $1 smoke/calibration, $9 text development including caller/judge, $4 audio, $4 held-out evaluation, $2 reserve requiring approval. Reported starting credit: $20; actual provider balance/expiry unverified.
- **Approved paid batches: 0. Recorded project provider usage: $0. Held reservations: $0. Estimated remaining credit: $20.** Pi conversation/research/review usage is separate from this project's API-key ledger.
- Every paid HTTP attempt reserves the model's full documented input context plus capped output, at uncached standard prices. Shared accounting includes agent, caller, judge and each retry; it does not use character-based token estimates as a hard bound.
- Decimal accounting, cross-process locking, atomic replacement and file/directory sync occur before dispatch. Missing/lost usage retains its full reservation. Invalid usage/model/tier or malformed successful responses halt further paid batches. A persisted pending request blocks later sends even if a halt write failed. There is no automatic release of uncertain spend.
- Hard maxima: 1,200 output tokens/request; 100 paid attempts/batch plus tighter dollar ceilings; 12 caller generations/episode; 8 tool rounds and 8 actual function calls/caller turn; ≤1 separately reserved HTTP retry (default 0); audio **0 seconds / 0 requests**. Batch limits can be lower. The first proposed batch uses four attempts, one caller turn, one tool step and zero retries.
- This is a project-side cap conditional on documented prices/model/tier/token limits, not a provider-console billing guarantee or accounting for another client/checkout. Unexpected provider behavior may already have incurred a charge before detection. Recheck prices and balance before future approvals.

### Actual verification and stop boundary

- Final command `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: **73 passed, 0 skipped, exit 0**. Cost tests mock HTTP; no project paid request was made. Final source hashes and receipt: `evidence/step5/checks-final-stop.json` and `unit-tests-final-stop.log`.
- Earlier Step 5 suite outputs are also retained: 66/66, 70/70 and 72/72. Review found atomic-halt, malformed-response, sync-order, mixed-local/paid-role and failed-halt-write risks; fixes have focused regressions, including cross-process/instance limits and global pending/halted interlocks. Review conversations are retained; they are not human adjudication or proof of provider billing behavior.
- Fresh CLI oracle saved at **`experiments/runs/m4_step5_oracle/`**: 10/10 exact CRM matches, zero model requests, language unjudged. Cost ledger batch IDs are included in new run manifests. This is a harness regression, not a model benchmark.
- All **196 pre-Step-5 experiment files** and **27 Step 4 evidence files** hash-match their receipts. `adjudication.json` is byte-identical to Step 4 and still pending human review; original M3 scores remain unchanged. User README and step-by-step prompt edits were not touched. `git diff --check` passed.

**Next paid action proposed, not approved:** `step5_smoke_001`, four synthetic text requests (caller, agent function request, agent tool-result reply, structured judge), no CRM writes/audio/phone. Uniform conservative bound **4 × $0.019920 = $0.079680**, under a **$0.10 authorization ceiling** drawn from smoke/calibration. Ask the user to approve this named batch and ceiling before changing its approval fields or making a paid request. Do not proceed to audio/held-out work or the next milestone step.

# Step 5 review resolution

Review scope: new budget module and model transport, their caller/judge/CLI integrations, runtime caller/tool caps, and offline cost tests. Previous Step 4 changes were not re-reviewed as a new feature. No project model request was sent.

## Concrete findings and fixes

1. **Failure + halt were separate ledger writes.** `fail(..., halt=True)` now records both in one locked atomic save. A competing reservation test confirms the next worker sees the halt, not an intermediate failed-but-open state.
2. **A successful HTTP response with a non-object JSON root did not halt.** Non-object roots now fail/halt atomically. JSON syntax/decode failures halt through the nonretryable error path. Full reservation stays held. Regression cases: `[]`, `null`, and invalid JSON.
3. **Atomic replacement alone was not a persistence barrier before dispatch.** Ledger saves now sync the file and parent directory while holding the lock. Tests assert sync → sync → HTTP ordering and no HTTP on either file-sync or directory-sync failure. This is not a physical power-loss test; OS/device semantics still apply.
4. **A shared paid-run ledger rejected a genuinely local caller.** Recognized loopback Ollama requests now use zero-provider-cost transport while retaining the run's caller/tool limits. A mixed local simulator/paid agent test checks that only the paid request consumes the currency ledger. Local cloud proxies are not authorized.
5. **A failed halt write could leave only a pending reservation.** The ledger now admits only one in-flight paid request, across all batches. Pending entries block later reservations. The regression injects a halt-write failure after the mocked paid response, restores I/O, then checks that a separate ledger instance cannot send again.
6. **Parent hardening:** a halted batch also blocks other approved batches until billing review. This prevents another pre-approved batch from proceeding with unresolved billing assumptions. Cross-batch regression added.

Tool-step rejection records the actual discarded model text and requested calls in the error trace. Tests count parallel calls, not only LLM/tool rounds. Budget refusals are tested as infrastructure/evaluation errors, with deterministic CRM state retained and reward unknown.

## Verification and review boundary

- Full deterministic suites: 66/66, then 70/70, then 72/72, finally **73/73**, no skips and exit 0. Every output/receipt is retained.
- Final tested Python-source hashes: `checks-final-stop.json`.
- The independent reviewer checked the first fixes and identified finding 5. Findings 5–6 were then fixed, inspected by the parent and tested; there was no additional independent post-fix approval. The review conversations are retained as evidence, not a human approval.
- No paid API, model availability, real usage, voice, phone, provider-console or physical crash test was run.

## Remaining bounds and risks

- Model-token arithmetic assumes the documented model/context, unchanged prices and requested default tier. A provider violating these assumptions could already have billed a different amount before the response is checked. This is not a provider-enforced billing cap.
- One canonical ledger cannot account for unrelated key use or copies/older restored ledgers. Operator edits must not run concurrently with workers. Approval records are not cryptographic proof of human authorization.
- The user's $20 balance/expiry is not authenticated. The selected text snapshot is deprecated and live access is unknown. No fallback is approved.
- Audio duration alone does not bound Realtime spend. Audio remains disabled, not provisionally covered by a guessed per-minute figure.
